senses.gloss: m.(b. h.; v. מָשַׁל I) [something tangible, substantial, plausible; cmp. אֲמַתְלָא,] a truth substantiated by an illustration, wise saying; fable, allegory; example; mashal. Cant. R. introd. אל יהי המ׳ הזח קל וכ׳ do not esteem the mashal lightly, for through it man gets at the basis of &c. Ib. יש לו מקרא ויש לו מ׳ וכ׳, v. מְלִיצָה.
units: <cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 40:4">Ex. R. s. 40</cite>, beg. <he>צריך אדם לחיות נוטל מ׳</he> man should take an example (of the Lord).
<cite ref="Pesachim 49a:22">Pes. 49ᵃ</cite> bot. <he>מ׳ לענבי וכ׳</he> it is like mixing grapes with &c.—<he>מ׳ למה הדבר דומה</he>, v. <cite ref="D00877"><he>דָּמָה</he></cite> a. preced.—
<cite ref="Bava Batra 15a:16">B. Bath. 15ᵃ</cite> <he>איוב לא היה … אלא מ׳ היה</he> the story of Job never occurred, but was invented merely as a parable.

Snh. 92ᵇ אמת מ׳ היה (the vision of the valley of the dead) was the truth of a mashal, (emended:) באמת מ׳ היה in the truth (the fact of resurrection) there was a symbol (for the redemption of Israel from captivity; Ez. XXXVII, 11).—

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot 4:4:6">Y. Keth. IV, 28ᶜ</cite> top; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 8:8:2">Y. Snh. VIII, 26ᶜ</cite> top <he>זה … שנאמרו בתורה במ׳</he> this is one of the three verses in which the Law uses metaphorical expressions (<cite ref="Exodus 21:19">Ex. XXI, 19</cite>; <cite ref="Exodus 22:2">XXII, 2</cite>; <cite ref="Deuteronomy 22:17">Deut. XXII, 17</cite>); Mekh. Mishp. 6; a. fr.—Pl. <he>מְשָׁלִים</he>, <he>מְשָׁלוֹת</he>.

<cite ref="Mishnah Sotah 9:15">Sot. IX, 15</cite> (<cite ref="Sotah 49a:7">49ᵃ</cite>) <he>משמת ר״מ בטלו מושלי מ׳</he> with the death of R. M. ceased the composers of fables. Cant. R. l. c. <he>מִשְׁלוֹתָיו של וכ׳</he> the wise sayings of Solomon. Ib. <he>דברי מ׳</he> didactic literature, opp. <he>זמר</he>. Ib. <he>שלש מ׳</he> three collections of sayings (<cite ref="Proverbs 1:6">Prov. I</cite> to IX; <cite ref="Proverbs 10">X</cite> to XXIV; <cite ref="Proverbs 25">XXV</cite> to XXXI).
<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 14:20">Num. R. s. 14</cite>, end <he>ועם בלעם … כי אם במ׳</he> God spoke to Balaam only through allegories (visions).—

<cite ref="Sukkah 28a:6">Succ. 28ᵃ</cite> <he>מִשְׁלוֹת שועלין</he> (Ms. M. <he>מִמְשְׁלוֹת</he>, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note) fox-fables; <he>מ׳ כובסין</he> washers’ fables; <cite ref="Bava Batra 134a">B. Bath. 134ᵃ</cite>.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 38b:22">Snh. 38ᵇ</cite> (Ms. M. <he>ממשלת</he>); <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 947:22">Yalk. Prov. 947</cite>.—
Gitt. 35ᵃ bot. ספר איוב ומִמְשָׁלוֹת copies of the Books of Job and Proverbs (v. infra).—מִשְׁלֵי (sub. שלמה) Mishlé, the Book of Proverbs (commencing with the word mishlé). Cant. R. l. c.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Yoma 1:8:2">Y. Yoma I, end, 39ᵇ</cite>; a. e.
